title: Spider-Man Was Buried Alive. Someone Took His Place.
canon: Kraven’s Last Hunt (1987), six-part Marvel Comics arc. Not a film recap.

lore_design.reason: Gothic pursuit: stone and rain for burial, warm lodge/city light for the impostor, restrained purple for psychological threat, and neutral daylight for aftermath. Trebuchet provides open readable letters; one family keeps labels consistent. The audience theater persists below a protected dark caption band.

u1.reason: Begin with the buried hero and an antagonist above him so both halves of the opening promise are visible.
elements: Coffin cross-section makes confinement clear; no claim that the comic shows this camera angle.
Tombstone and soil establish burial; restrained rain supports the Gothic setting.

u2.reason: The source cover carries recognition; plum echoes its printed title without recoloring the artwork.
elements: Registered publisher cover identifies the actual comic collection; date refers to the original story, not this later collected edition.

u3.reason: A warm trophy-room diagram explains the hunter’s identity and the stolen costume.
elements: Lion-pattern vest, moustache and broad silhouette identify Kraven.
Black-and-white suit stays distinct from the red/blue Spider-Man film costume.

u4.reason: Amber city windows establish the impostor’s night patrol; this is warm city light, not a claim of a fire.
elements: Recognizable black suit and a small Kraven identity inset explain who is inside.

u5.reason: Concrete and bars explain the captured monster; visual proof replaces another portrait.
elements: Rat-like ears and tail identify Vermin; the containment is illustrative staging.

u6.reason: Muted earth and a restrained red field mark danger as the hand and body break the soil plane.
elements: Shared grave geometry links the escape to the opening.
Body emergence shows a meaningful state change rather than a floating portrait.

u7.reason: Return to the same warm lodge palette, changing the framing to show the unequal confrontation.
elements: Peter reaches toward Kraven while the hunter’s arms remain down.

u8.reason: A closer purple-toned threat beat separates the final test from the earlier capture.
elements: The same Vermin identity returns for a sourced reason; this is a deliberate story callback, not another episode’s filler.

u9.reason: A quiet neutral aftermath prevents the ending from celebrating the hunter’s death.
elements: Confession letter and an absent chair suggest the consequence without reenacting a death.
